ownership_reason: Only the gold reads a control's value and decides the pairs a named control submits: hops 1, 2 and 4 pass the controls and the list along, and hop 3 only decides whether a control takes part (form-submittable tag, not disabled, a non-empty name) and reads its name. Once the gold has added (six, "") for the textarea, 'six=seven' can appear only if a caller rewrites the gold's output, mutates the control, or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises that any control other than a select box or a checkable control submits one pair with its value; the value of a textarea is its text, which the variant drops. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Element.val() ('Get the value of a form element (input, textarea, etc)': the text for a textarea, the 'value' attribute otherwise), its setter Element.val(String) and Elements.val(); ElementsTest::val passes ("two" for <textarea>two</textarea>), as do the chain's other form tests (usesOnForCheckboxValueIfNoValueSet, adoptedFormsRetainInputs, controlsAddedAfterParseAreLinkedWithForms, removeFormElement).
